reflection.text:
Epothilone B unblinded as Tubulin stabiliser / Microtubule stabilizers - our protocol call Microtubule stabilizers p=0.92 was correct, verdict correct, scientist_correct true. Calibration was appropriate given strength and consistency of evidence, budget exhausted 0/4 wells left.

What got it right: The extreme, monotonic tubulin-bundling signature was discriminative from the first acquisitions. Well w_b414b296e0 at 0.1 uM rep1 (e2) already showed tub_std z=+33.1, tub_glcm_contrast z=+28.0, tub_mean z=+18.3, and well w_82fe9cfd0d at 1 uM rep1 (e3) amplified to z=+117.6 / +87.2 / +58.7. This was not a subtle shift in mean intensity alone but a texture/std increase consistent with bundles/halos, which describe_phenotype on 4 fields (e4) phrased as density lower vs DMSO and candidates: Microtubule stabilizers, i.e. bright bundles rather than depolymerization/loss of tubulin seen with destabilizers.

compare_to_reference_atlas (e5) over 2 wells gave NSC 2/2 Microtubule stabilizers, k-neighbours 6/10 stabilizers, 4/10 Eg5 inhibitors. That second-place Eg5 tally could have misled - Eg5 inhibitors share mitotic arrest and cell count drop - but tubulin texture/std magnitude separates them: Eg5/Aurora produce monopolar/multipolar spindles without the massive microtubule mass/bundling increase. Our update_hypotheses 0.88 stabilizers (e6) correctly down-weighted Eg5 to 0.05 despite k-neighbour overlap.

Extensions strengthened the call. Adding w_2e25395163 at 0.3 uM (e7) z=+154.7 contrast, +77.4 std and w_54b0bc6ac3 at 0.03 uM (e8) z=+10.1 std / +10.0 contrast captured onset and maximal effect. Dose_response (e10) rho=+1.00 for tub_std over 4 wells/4 doses and (e11) rho=-1.00 for cell_count - monotonic increase in tubulin bundling with monotonic cell loss - is the expected pharmacology for suppression of microtubule dynamics associated with mitotic arrest described for epothilone B PMID 14522931 and for epothilones as a microtubule-stabilizing class with taxol-like mechanism PMID 7757983, also reflected in recent structural work PMID 41224993 and microtubule stabilization studies PMID 29348323 PMID 41673684. That dose-response discriminates stabilizers from destabilizers, which would show decreased tub_mean/std at high dose, and from Aurora/Actin classes which lack this tubulin dose-response.

Second atlas comparison (e9) over 4 wells remained NSC 3/4 stabilizers with 6/10 stabilizers, 3/10 destabilizers, 1/10 Eg5 in k-neighbours. The single dissenting well at 0.03 uM was correctly interpreted as weak onset: per protocol per_well similarity 0.401 to Microtubule destabilizers vs 0.63-0.894 to stabilizers at 0.1-1.0 uM, summed similarity 2.386 vs 0.401. Treating that as low-dose noise rather than contradictory evidence was correct; acquisition choice to include a low dose rather than only high doses made this interpretable.

What could have misled / limits: Spearman p=0 in e10/e11 is a reporting truncation with n=4, not true p=0, and with single replicate per dose (all rep1) we had no within-dose variance. Budget forced sampling 0.03-1 uM; we did not acquire 0.001-0.01 uM or 3 uM, so EC50/plateau not defined and very-high-dose toxicity not probed. The initial 4/10 Eg5 k-neighbour signal and later 3/10 destabilizer k-neighbour signal illustrate reference overlap in mitotic arrest space - reliance on NSC alone without texture/std and dose-response would be fragile. search_literature 'microtubule stabilizer phenotype tubulin bundling mitotic arrest microscopy' returned 0 hits (e17), so we had no atlas-independent phenotype ontology to cite beyond e4.

Next run: this acquisition order - mid dose 0.1 uM to detect onset, high dose 1 uM for maximal phenotype, then interpolate 0.3 and 0.03 uM for dose-response - was efficient. For future blinded runs, retain the same tub_std / tub_glcm_contrast / tub_mean triad plus cell_count dose-response, and NSC per-well similarities to quantify onset vs maximal votes, before increasing probability >0.9.
